box on the bottom of the stack, as well as ones in the middle, but not the ones at the top. Why?
The law of moment of force states that force is equal to mass times acceleration. When you lift one box, you will accelerate downwards, with an acceleration that depends on how much force you are applying to the box. Bending at the knees will help you apply a greater force to the box, so you will accelerate to a greater extent, making it easier to pick up the box at the bottom of the stack. On the other hand, with bent knees you will also apply greater force to the box at the top, making picking that up also easier. It doesn't matter that you will accelerate to the same extent as for the bottom box: accelerating upwards will also help you lift that box. In the absence of any external force, you will accelerate to the same extent as you will for the bottom box,
